title: In-person mutual attestation
summary: Two people meet, confirm each other, and each issues the other a credential. No third party, no ordering, no network — and the credentials may move long afterwards.

first-person.description: One of the two people present. The name distinguishes the two roles; it does not order them.

attest-first.description: Delivers the credential this party issues about the other. Anchor-rooted, not following any step: it is simultaneous with attest-second, and neither precedes the other.

attest-second.description: The mirror of attest-first. Expressing this pair as a chain would invent an ordering the meeting does not have; expressing it as mutual prev would be a cycle.

anchor.derivation: A value the two parties establish while together and which neither could have produced alone — a scanned code, a key agreement, a compared short authentication string. The enactment identifier is derived from it, so both steps signing `ceremony.enactment` commit to the same anchor without either step committing to the other.

sideEffects.rationale: Each party mints a credential about the other. Neither is compensatable by this ceremony; revocation is the issuer's own business.

exposure.rationale: Each step delivers credential material the other party retains, and each party issues on their own authority about a person present. `enactmentPrivacy` is blinded because the anchor would otherwise be a durable correlation handle across two credentials meant to stand alone.

org.example.proximity.note: Illustrative only — the framework reserves no namespace and gives this none. A real deployment would use a namespace it controls.
